chapter: Lessons, WPA band and sidemen years
title: Jobs with Bunk Johnson, Bill Matthews, Freddie Coleman and Kid Howard
summary: He played the Paddock, Mardi Gras lounge and other jobs with various leaders.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well then I played around the city. I played with D.D. and Billy a while, and Ernest Rogers, and I played with, that was during the WPA time. I played, I played a job with Bunk Johnson and George Lewis.

Well I remember hearing down the country violin. Yeah. I remember later Bunk said he'd like for you to be, wish you could have gone to New York and played with him once. Yeah. So you told me that one time. He'd like to use you on clarinet.
Well then I played around Boydman Street. Played out there with Bill Matthews. And continued on playing with Bill Matthews now when he had dates, you know. Yeah.
I remember hearing you at the paddock quite often there.
Yeah, I played at the paddock.
Some nights you'd be there on the Tuesday night when they'd take a night off, you'd be there quite regularly for a long time.

Yeah, well, I played at the paddock with Bill Matthews and I played there with Thomas Jefferson. And I played at the paddock with Freddie Coleman and we left the paddock and went down to the Mardi Gras. Played down at the Mardi Gras with Freddie Coleman. You're a member of his band then.
I forgot that. Were you there quite a while at the Mardi Gras then?
Yeah. Yeah. I worked there just about, maybe about a month or about six weeks in there or something like that. And I played at the Mardi Gras with Kid Howard's band on Tuesday night.
